findings.construct: pub struct RouteWorkflow { pub id: String, pub status: String, pub is_validated: bool, pub is_sent: bool, pub sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> }
findings.problem: RouteWorkflow uses raw String fields and lifecycle booleans that allow illegal state combinations (e.g., status="sent", is_sent=false, is_validated=false simultaneously). No invariants are enforced.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct RouteWorkflow with contradictory lifecycle flags, causing silent misrouting or double-sent behavior at runtime
findings.fix: Replace status/is_validated/is_sent with a single RouteState enum where each variant owns its lifecycle data (e.g., RouteState::Validated, RouteState::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }).

findings.problem: status is a free-form String instead of a typed enum. Any string value is accepted, including meaningless values like "foo" or "SENT" that do not correspond to real workflow states.
findings.failure_mode: Pattern matches on status string are fallible; typos or unexpected values cause logic errors or panics at the match site instead of compile-time guarantees
findings.fix: Define enum RouteState { Pending, Validated, Sent } and replace status: String with state: RouteState.

findings.problem: is_validated is a bare bool lifecycle flag. Booleans provide no ordering, no directionality, and no guarantee that validation precedes other transitions. Combined with is_sent, they form a fragile two-bit state machine.
findings.failure_mode: Validation and send flags can become inconsistent (e.g., is_validated=false but is_sent=true), violating the required ordering invariant that routes must be validated before sending
findings.fix: Encode validation as a variant of RouteState enum. Remove is_validated bool entirely.

findings.problem: is_sent is a bare bool lifecycle flag alongside is_validated, forming an unenforced two-bit state machine. No transition logic prevents invalid state combinations.
findings.failure_mode: Route can be marked sent without being validated, or sent twice, because the bool pair allows (false,false), (true,false), (false,true), (true,true) without enforcing a DAG
findings.fix: Encode sent as RouteState::Sent variant that owns sent_at_epoch_ms. The enum ensures sent is reached only via a Validated predecessor.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is an optional field separate from the lifecycle booleans. This means a route can be sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(123) while is_sent=false, or vice versa. Optional lifecycle data must live inside the variant that owns it.
findings.failure_mode: Timestamp is accessible even when the route is not in the sent state, allowing callers to read sent timestamps for non-sent routes
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the RouteState::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } variant where it is only accessible when the route is actually sent.

findings.problem: Route identifier is a raw String with no domain semantics. Any string is accepted, including empty strings, whitespace, or values that are not valid route IDs.
findings.failure_mode: Routes can be created with empty or malformed IDs, causing lookup failures, duplicate routes, or silent identity collisions in downstream systems
findings.fix: Define a RouteId newtype with a smart constructor that validates non-empty format, or at minimum use a non-empty string wrapper type.

findings.construct: pub struct RouteWorkflow { pub id: String, pub status: String, ... }
findings.problem: Raw primitives (String for id and status) cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors. Callers can construct invalid domain states directly without any validation at the boundary.
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted input (empty ids, invalid status strings) reaches core logic without any gate, because there is no parse_boundary function that validates and converts external strings into trusted domain types
findings.fix: Add fn RouteWorkflow::parse(id: &str, state: &str) -> Result<RouteWorkflow, RouteError> that validates inputs once at the boundary and returns typed errors.

findings.construct: pub fn mark_sent(mut item: RouteWorkflow) -> RouteWorkflow
findings.problem: mark_sent takes and returns the struct by value, mutating fields directly with item.status = "sent". This leaks domain mutation into the public API and allows arbitrary callers to transition state without validation or audit.
findings.failure_mode: Any code can call mark_sent on any RouteWorkflow regardless of whether it was in a valid predecessor state (e.g., Validated), bypassing state-machine guards entirely
findings.fix: Replace with fn RouteWorkflow::mark_sent(self) -> Result<RouteWorkflow, RouteError> that checks the current variant is Validated before transitioning to Sent.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or RouteWorkflow lifecycle operations
no profiler evidence for struct layout or cache-line behavior of RouteWorkflow
no allocation evidence — mark_sent performs to_string allocation on every call
no command-truth evidence for any CLI or integration command that exercises RouteWorkflow
residual_risk: Struct has no typestate guards, allowing any caller to construct illegal state combinations via direct field access. The mark_sent function has no pre-condition checks, making it a silent state-violation vector. Public fields prevent even encapsulation-level validation. Without enum typestate, newtype ID, and smart constructor boundary, the domain model is fully reversible to illegal states by any mutation.
